acumatica.name: Acumatica
acumatica.description: Acumatica Cloud ERP through the contract-based REST endpoint, with a shared session so the licence is not spent on logins.

fields.name: instanceUrl
fields.label: Instance URL
fields.instructions: No trailing path — Erpy adds the endpoint itself.

fields.name: endpointVersion
fields.label: Endpoint version
fields.instructions: From System → Integration → Web Service Endpoints. Use the Default endpoint’s version.

fields.label: Sign in
fields.instructions: Use a dedicated integration user. Acumatica counts concurrent sessions against your licence, and sharing a person’s login means their password change breaks the storefront.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: company
fields.label: Company / tenant
fields.instructions: Leave blank on a single-tenant instance.

fields.name: branch
fields.label: Branch
fields.instructions: Leave blank to use the user’s default branch.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.label: Warehouse
fields.instructions: The warehouse stock is read from and orders are raised against.

fields.name: orderType
fields.label: Sales order type
fields.instructions: The order type new orders are created as.

fields.name: holdNewOrders
fields.label: Create orders on hold
fields.instructions: On is the safe default: an order on hold can be reviewed before it is committed to a warehouse.

afas.name: AFAS Profit
afas.description: AFAS Profit through GetConnectors and UpdateConnectors, with every connector and field name configurable — because in AFAS they always are.

fields.name: environmentId
fields.label: Environment ID
fields.instructions: The number in your AFAS URL. Erpy builds the REST host from it.

fields.name: token
fields.label: App Connector token
fields.instructions: Paste the token value only — the part between <data> and </data> in the XML AFAS gave you. Erpy wraps and encodes it.

fields.label: GetConnectors
fields.instructions: AFAS has no fixed schema: a GetConnector is built by your implementation partner. These are the names AFAS’s own standard connectors use — change any that differ, and correct individual field names on the mapping screen.

fields.name: modifiedField
fields.label: Modified field
fields.instructions: Used for delta syncs. Leave blank if your connectors do not expose one — every sync then reads everything, which Erpy’s change detection makes cheap.

fields.name: orderReferenceField
fields.label: Order reference field
fields.instructions: The field on the sales orders GetConnector that holds the customer reference (RfCs), where Erpy writes the Commerce order number. Order status is matched on it, and it is checked before an order is created so a retry cannot post the same order twice.

fields.name: salesOrderConnector
fields.label: UpdateConnector
fields.instructions: The UpdateConnector new sales orders are posted to.

mock.name: Mock ERP
mock.description: A pretend ERP with deterministic data. Use it to try the mapping and sync screens, or to prove a problem is in the connector rather than in Erpy.

fields.name: itemCount
fields.label: Items to invent
fields.instructions: How many products, prices and stock lines this pretend ERP holds.

fields.name: failEvery
fields.label: Fail every Nth record
fields.instructions: For trying out the dead-letter screen. Zero never fails.

exact-online.name: Exact Online
exact-online.description: Exact Online through the REST API, with the OAuth consent step and the rotating refresh token handled for you.

fields.name: region
fields.label: Region
fields.instructions: Exact runs a separate installation per country and they do not share data. Pick the one your login belongs to.

fields.label: App registration
fields.instructions: Register an app in the Exact App Centre and set its redirect URI to exactly the value below — Exact compares it character for character.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: division
fields.label: Division
fields.instructions: The numeric division code. Leave blank and it is looked up from the login’s current division once per run — but set it explicitly before going live: the current division is whichever one the user last opened in Exact, and a wrong division returns an empty, entirely successful response.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.label: Warehouse code
fields.instructions: Stock is read from this warehouse. Leave blank for the company total.

business-central.name: Dynamics 365 Business Central
business-central.description: Microsoft’s mid-market ERP, through the standard API v2.0 and an Entra ID app registration.

fields.label: Entra ID application
fields.instructions: Register an application in Entra ID, grant it the Business Central API permission, then grant the resulting application access inside Business Central itself under Microsoft Entra Applications.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.label: Tenant ID
fields.instructions: The GUID of your Microsoft 365 tenant.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: environment
fields.label: Environment name
fields.instructions: As it appears in the Business Central admin centre — “Production”, “Sandbox”, or whatever yours is called.

fields.name: companyName
fields.label: Company
fields.instructions: The Business Central company to read and write. Leave the display name exactly as it appears in the company list.

fields.label: Optional endpoints
fields.instructions: Business Central’s standard API does not expose sales prices or posted shipment tracking numbers. If you need either, publish a page as an API in your own extension and name it here; leave blank and Erpy will simply not sync that entity.

fields.name: pricesEndpoint
fields.label: Sales prices endpoint
fields.instructions: Relative to the company. Must expose itemNo, unitPrice, and optionally customerNo, customerPriceGroup, minimumQuantity, startingDate and endingDate.

fields.name: shipmentsEndpoint
fields.label: Posted shipments endpoint
fields.instructions: Relative to the company. Must expose orderNo, no and lastModifiedDateTime (the record’s SystemModifiedAt, which delta syncs filter on), and optionally externalDocumentNo, packageTrackingNo, shippingAgentCode and postingDate.

myob-acumatica.name: MYOB Acumatica (Advanced)
myob-acumatica.description: MYOB Acumatica — previously MYOB Advanced — through the contract-based REST endpoint.

fields.name: endpointVersion
fields.label: Endpoint version
fields.instructions: From Integration → Web Service Endpoints, using the Default endpoint.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

myob-exo.name: MYOB Exo
myob-exo.description: MYOB Exo Business through the Exo API gateway.

fields.name: apiUrl
fields.label: API URL
fields.instructions: The hosted gateway, or your own Exo API host for an on-premise deployment.

fields.label: Credentials
fields.instructions: Exo needs three separate things and gives the same 401 when any one is missing.

fields.name: developerKey
fields.label: Developer key
fields.instructions: Identifies your integration. Sent as x-myobapi-key.

fields.name: exoPassword
fields.label: Exo password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: accountUser
fields.label: MYOB account email
fields.instructions: Only needed on a hosted install, where the gateway also wants Basic credentials.

fields.name: accountPassword
fields.label: MYOB account password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: locationId
fields.label: Stock location
fields.instructions: The numeric location id stock is read from.

odoo.name: Odoo
odoo.description: Odoo Community or Enterprise through the external JSON-RPC API, using an API key rather than a password.

fields.name: database
fields.label: Database
fields.instructions: On Odoo Online this is usually the subdomain.

fields.name: username
fields.label: Login
fields.instructions: The email address of a dedicated integration user.

fields.name: apiKey
fields.label: API key
fields.instructions: Generate one under the user’s Preferences → Account Security. An API key works everywhere a password does and can be revoked on its own.

fields.name: warehouseId
fields.label: Warehouse ID
fields.instructions: The numeric id of the stock location stock is read from. Leave blank for all internal locations.

fields.name: pricelistId
fields.label: Base pricelist ID
fields.instructions: Usually your public pricelist. Its items are left out of contract pricing — the Commerce base price comes from each product’s Sales Price. Every other pricelist becomes contract pricing.

fields.name: salesTeamId
fields.label: Sales team ID
fields.instructions: Optional. Web orders are often given their own team so they can be reported on separately.

fields.name: confirmOrders
fields.label: Confirm orders on arrival
fields.instructions: Off leaves them as quotations for someone to review. On confirms them, which reserves stock immediately.

netsuite.name: NetSuite
netsuite.description: Oracle NetSuite through SuiteTalk REST, with bulk reads done in SuiteQL so a large catalogue does not take all night.

fields.label: Account
fields.instructions: Setup → Company → Company Information shows your account id. A sandbox looks like 1234567_SB1.

fields.label: Token-Based Authentication
fields.instructions: Create an integration record under Setup → Integration → Manage Integrations with Token-Based Authentication enabled, then create an access token for it under Setup → Users/Roles → Access Tokens. NetSuite shows each secret once and never again.

fields.name: consumerKey
fields.label: Consumer key
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: consumerSecret
fields.label: Consumer secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: tokenId
fields.label: Token ID
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: tokenSecret
fields.label: Token secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: subsidiaryId
fields.label: Subsidiary internal ID
fields.instructions: Required on OneWorld accounts. Leave blank on a single-subsidiary account.

fields.name: locationId
fields.label: Location internal ID
fields.instructions: The location orders are raised against, and the one stock is read from.

fields.name: itemTypes
fields.label: Item types to sync
fields.instructions: NetSuite item types, comma separated. Service and other non-sellable types are usually best left out.

fields.name: categoryField
fields.label: Item category field
fields.instructions: The id of a custom item field holding the product category, if you have one. Leave blank and no category is read — NetSuite refuses a whole query that names a field the account does not have.

fields.name: orderReferenceField
fields.label: Order reference field
fields.instructions: Orders Erpy creates are matched by their External ID. Only name a custom transaction body field here if another integration also raises web orders and keeps the Commerce order number in it.

fields.name: orderApproved
fields.label: Create orders already approved
fields.instructions: Off means orders land pending approval, which is what most finance teams want to start with.

priority.name: Priority
priority.description: Priority ERP through its OData interface, with every form name configurable because no two Priority installations are alike.

fields.name: serverUrl
fields.label: Priority server URL
fields.instructions: The host only — Erpy adds the OData path.

fields.name: company
fields.label: Company
fields.instructions: The Priority company (database) name, as it appears in the OData URL.

fields.name: tabulaIni
fields.label: Configuration file
fields.instructions: Almost always tabula.ini. Change it only if your installation says otherwise.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.label: Forms
fields.instructions: Priority exposes its screens rather than an abstracted API, and installations differ. These are the standard names; change any that your implementation renamed.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.label: Warehouse
fields.instructions: Stock is read from this warehouse. Leave blank to read every warehouse.

fields.name: priceList
fields.label: Price list
fields.instructions: The price list new orders are raised against.

sage-200.name: Sage 200
sage-200.description: Sage 200 Standard and Professional through the Sage 200 API.

fields.name: edition
fields.label: Edition
fields.instructions: The two editions answer on different API paths. UK and Irish companies use the same ones.

fields.label: Sage application
fields.instructions: Register an app on the Sage developer portal and set its callback to exactly the value below.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: subscriptionKey
fields.label: Subscription key
fields.instructions: The Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key from your Sage developer account. It identifies the application, not the customer.

fields.name: siteId
fields.label: Site ID
fields.instructions: Sent as the X-Site header. Without it a perfectly authenticated request returns nothing rather than an error.

sage-accounting.name: Sage Business Cloud Accounting
sage-accounting.description: Sage Accounting. Syncs products and contacts, and posts completed orders into the ledger as sales invoices — it has no sales orders or stock of its own.

fields.label: Sage application
fields.instructions: Register an app on the Sage developer portal and set its callback to exactly the value below.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: region
fields.label: Country
fields.instructions: The country of the Sage business. It picks the Sage sign-in the Connect button opens.

fields.label: Posting orders
fields.instructions: Sage Accounting has no sales order object, so a completed Commerce order is posted as a sales invoice.

fields.name: ledgerAccountId
fields.label: Sales ledger account
fields.instructions: The ledger account id invoice lines are posted to. Leave blank to use the product’s own.

fields.name: taxRateId
fields.label: Default tax rate
fields.instructions: Used when a line has no tax rate of its own. Sage will refuse an invoice line without one.

sage-intacct.name: Sage Intacct
sage-intacct.description: Sage Intacct through the XML gateway, with its two-part authentication and resultId paging handled for you.

fields.label: Web services sender
fields.instructions: Issued to the integration by Sage, not by the customer. The same sender id is used across every Intacct company you connect to.

fields.name: senderPassword
fields.label: Sender password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.label: Company login
fields.instructions: A web services user in the customer’s Intacct company. It must be a Web Services user, not a normal one, and the sender id has to be authorised under Company → Security → Web Services Authorizations.

fields.name: userPassword
fields.label: User password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: entityId
fields.label: Entity
fields.instructions: For multi-entity companies. Leave blank to work at the top level.

fields.label: Objects
fields.instructions: Which Intacct objects to read. The defaults suit a company running Order Entry and Inventory Control; change them if yours is configured differently.

fields.name: orderDocumentType
fields.label: Sales order document type
fields.instructions: The Order Entry transaction definition new orders are created as. It must match exactly, including capitalisation.

sage-x3.name: Sage X3
sage-x3.description: Sage X3 through the REST web services, addressing its representations directly.

fields.name: serverUrl
fields.label: X3 server URL
fields.instructions: Include the port the Syracuse web server listens on.

fields.name: folder
fields.label: Folder
fields.instructions: The X3 folder. The same credentials against a different folder are a different dataset entirely.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.label: Representations
fields.instructions: The X3 representations to read. These are the standard ones; change any that your implementation replaced with a custom representation.

fields.name: salesSite
fields.label: Sales site
fields.instructions: The X3 site orders are raised against, and the one stock is read from.

sap-business-one.name: SAP Business One
sap-business-one.description: SAP Business One through the Service Layer, with one shared session so the licence is not spent on logins.

fields.name: serviceLayerUrl
fields.label: Service Layer URL
fields.instructions: Include the /b1s/v1 path. Port 50000 is the default for the Service Layer.

fields.name: password
fields.label: Password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.label: Warehouse code
fields.instructions: Stock is read from this warehouse and order lines are raised against it. Leave blank for the company-wide figure.

fields.name: priceListNum
fields.label: Base price list number
fields.instructions: The list whose prices become the Commerce base price. Other B1 price lists are not synced; customer-specific prices come from Special Prices for Business Partners.

fields.name: seriesNumber
fields.label: Document series
fields.instructions: The numbering series new sales orders use. Leave blank for the default.

fields.name: ignoreSslErrors
fields.label: This Service Layer uses a self-signed certificate
fields.instructions: Turns off certificate verification for this connection only — the login and every request. Leave off unless you know it does: it usually means an on-premise install that has never had a real certificate, and a real one is the better fix.

unit4.name: Unit4 ERP
unit4.description: Unit4 ERPx and Business World. Every resource path is configurable, because no two Unit4 estates expose the same one.

fields.name: baseUrl
fields.label: API base URL
fields.instructions: Everything up to but not including the resource name.

fields.name: company
fields.label: Company
fields.instructions: Sent as the companyId parameter on every request.

fields.name: tokenUrl
fields.label: Token endpoint
fields.instructions: Required for OAuth. Your Unit4 Identity Services token URL.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret / password
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.label: Resources
fields.instructions: Unit4 estates differ. These are the ERPx conventions — change any that your deployment names differently, and correct individual field names on the mapping screen.

fields.name: modifiedSinceParam
fields.label: Changed-since parameter
fields.instructions: The query parameter your estate filters on for records changed since a moment, sent with a UTC timestamp on every delta sync. Ask your implementation partner what yours is called. Leave blank if there is none: every sync then reads everything, which is slower but misses nothing.

fields.name: probeResource
fields.label: Resource to test with
fields.instructions: Used by the Test button. Any resource this user can read.

visma-net.name: Visma.net ERP
visma-net.description: Visma.net ERP (Financials) through the integration API, authenticated with Visma Connect.

fields.label: Visma Connect
fields.instructions: Register an integration in Visma Developer Portal and grant it the Visma.net ERP scope for the customer’s tenant.

fields.name: clientSecret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.instructions: Store this in an environment variable rather than in the database.

fields.name: scope
fields.label: Scope
fields.instructions: The scopes granted to your integration. Read-only installations can drop the create scope.

fields.name: companyId
fields.label: Company ID
fields.instructions: Sent as the ipp-company-id header. A wrong one returns an empty, entirely successful response rather than an error.
